title: Brand-Isolated Interaction Color Ramps for Dark Console (charts, tables, buttons)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Brand accents bleed in dark mode when used across interactive micro-states (hover, focus, active) and data overlays (table row highlights, chart series glows). Current token set uses a single accent ramp per brand that assumes a light background; when placed on deep surfaces it loses contrast or oversaturates adjacent UI elements.

Goal: Define a brand-isolated interaction ramp and a small set of scoped component overrides that produce predictable, accessible micro-interaction colors across dark console surfaces. The solution should: produce consistent perceived brightness across different brand hues, preserve text and icon contrast against interactive surfaces, avoid color contamination in adjacent grayscale surfaces, and be computationally light to generate at build/runtime.

Scope: buttons, pill badges, table row highlights, table cell selection, chart series fills/glows, small focus rings and hover states. This ticket covers token definitions and a reference Figma kit and a PRD for the frontend implementation; engineering work to wire tokens into runtime will be a follow-up linked as dependencies.

Deliverables:
- Token spec: new token names and mapping rules (brand isolation ramp tokens + semantic aliases).
- Figma component kit with annotated dark-surface variants and visual QA for 6 brand hues.
- Frontend override guidance: CSS var mapping, component API flag (useIsolatedAccent: boolean), and suggested fallbacks for older browsers.
- Accessibility acceptance criteria (contrast ratios and motion-friendly transitions).

Design decisions and approach:
1) Isolation via desaturated overlay method: generate ramps by compositing a desaturated overlay layer + small luminance adjustment rather than purely adjusting hue saturation/lightness. This preserves chroma information while providing predictable perceived darkness on deep surfaces.
2) Per-component semantic aliases: define tokens like token.interaction.brandAccent.surfaceHover/active/focus; components map to semantic tokens rather than raw brand color tokens.
3) Small, deterministic algorithm for runtime: start from brand base color (hex), compute a neutral-desaturate factor and blend with surface-luminance anchor to yield three micro-state colors. This allows runtime compatibility when brands are customer-provided.
4) Chart-specific treatment: chart glows should use a single-channel alpha overlay of the brandAccent with a blurred gaussian mask and a tuned luminance delta to avoid overwhelming axes/labels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hover/Active/Focus for primary and subtle buttons maintain WCAG AA text/icon contrast (>=4.5:1 for any icon/text on that surface).
- Table row highlight and chart series glow do not reduce neighboring text below AA when applied at default opacity.
- Figma QA for six selected brand hues (red, green, blue, purple, orange, teal) shows consistent perceived lightness across examples.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Using a desaturated composite increases maintenance compared to hand-tuned ramps but scales to many brand hues and supports customer-provided brand colors.
- Slight chroma loss for very low-saturation brand tokens is acceptable; we will document a recommended minimum brand saturation for reliable results.

Next steps / Implementation plan:
- Deliver Figma kit and annotated token spec (this ticket).
- Frontend engineering ticket (ENG-98412) to implement runtime generator and component flagging; will be dependent.
- QA pass with accessibility team and solutions engineers for customer-provided brand tests.
